artists.biography: North Sea Radio Orchestra (generally abbreviated to NSRO) is a British contemporary music ensemble and cross-disciplinary chamber orchestra (plus chorus). Set up mainly as a vehicle for the compositions of its musical director, Craig Fortnam, it has also performed works by William D. Drake and James Larcombe. The ensemble is notable for its post-modern fusion of Romantic music and later twentieth century forms, and for its bridging of the worlds of contemporary classical music, British folk music, London art-rock and poetry (setting music to poems by W.B. Yeats, Thomas Hardy, Alfred Lord Tennyson and Daniel Dundas Maitland). Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Dronne, released in 2016 on The Household Mark label, is the fourth studio album by North Sea Radio Orchestra, a British ensemble known for blending elements of rock, folk, world, and country music with chamber and progressive influences. The album showcases a richly textured musical style that draws on a wide historical palette, incorporating traces of Purcell, Victorian parlour music, Britten, sea shanties, and krautrock, resulting in a sound described by Prog magazine as "particularly inspired" and akin to "a core sample drilled down through the last few hundred years of music". This eclectic mix reflects the band's signature approach of combining classical instrumentation with contemporary and traditional folk elements.

In the context of North Sea Radio Orchestra's discography, Dronne follows their 2011 album I a Moon and precedes the 2019 Folly Bololey project. It continues the group's exploration of intricate arrangements and pastoral themes, further establishing their niche within progressive folk and chamber pop genres. Critically, the album was well received for its lush, gentle soundscapes and inventive compositions, with the accompanying End of Chimes EP praised as "a highly entertaining discovery" and "gentle, lush and frankly beguiling". While not a mainstream commercial hit, Dronne solidified North Sea Radio Orchestra's reputation for sophisticated, genre-blending music that appeals to a discerning audience.
